llm.summary: The local workflow has limited access, but its helper does not verify medical claims and the optional Windows app needs separate review.

dimensions.detail: The script reads the selected input and writes a report to the selected output directory. It contains no network calls, credential access, broad indexing, or background workers.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The Python workflow uses only the standard library. A separate unsigned Windows installer is explicitly optional and never automatically downloaded or run. Its [publisher release](https://github.com/rapidworker1/Multiple-AI-models-Toolkit/releases/tag/Main) describes a general AI app; the executable was not inspected.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions require provider review, prohibit clinical protocols and fabricated claims, and leave publication to the practice. No hidden automatic actions were found.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The bundled workflow creates or overwrites treatment-brief.md under the chosen output directory. It installs no services, scheduled tasks, or persistent agent instructions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Drafting instructions fit the stated purpose, but the script only checks field presence and length. The supplied template also lacks the fields it expects.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use this as drafting assistance, not a medical or compliance validator. Have the licensed provider verify claims before publication. Choose the output folder carefully because an existing report is overwritten. The optional Windows app is unnecessary for the Python workflow and needs independent review; matching its supplied hash does not establish safety.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The SkillSpector advisory identifies a real functionality gap: the helper neither drafts pages nor checks clinical evidence. This is downgraded to a quality limitation because the agent receives drafting instructions and publication remains subject to provider review.
[LP3] expected: The SkillSpector concern is not supported as excess authority: report writing is disclosed and directed by --out. Missing tool-scope metadata alone does not establish unsafe access.
